group.title: Travel and holidays
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: To arrive at a hotel or airport and show your booking so you can stay or fly.
examples: We {checked in} at the hotel just after lunch.
wrong: We checked in at the hotel as we were leaving it for good.

words.meaning: The area at an airport where you collect your bags after a flight.
examples: We waited at {baggage claim} for our suitcases.
wrong: We left our bags at baggage claim before getting on the plane.

words.meaning: A seat on a plane or train next to the walkway between rows.
examples: I always ask for an {aisle seat} so I can stretch my legs.
wrong: From my aisle seat I had the best view out of the window.

words.meaning: A seat on a plane, bus or train next to the window.
examples: She took the {window seat} to watch the mountains.
wrong: I chose the window seat because I couldn’t see outside from it.

words.meaning: A place where people can put up tents and stay outdoors.
examples: We put up our tent at a {campsite} near the lake.
wrong: The campsite was a hotel room on the tenth floor.

words.meaning: A person or company whose job is to plan and sell trips for people.
examples: Our {travel agent} found us a cheap flight to Spain.
wrong: The travel agent fixed our car engine before the trip.

words.meaning: In or to a country across the sea.
examples: My cousin moved {overseas} to work in Canada.
wrong: She went overseas to the shop at the end of her street.

words.meaning: The natural things you see in a place, such as hills, rivers and forests.
examples: The {scenery} on the coast road was beautiful.
wrong: We admired the scenery by closing our eyes for the whole drive.

words.meaning: A place or thing that many visitors come to see.
examples: The old castle is the town’s main {tourist attraction}.
wrong: The tourist attraction was so dull that no visitor ever went there.

words.meaning: A holiday where flights, hotel and sometimes meals are sold together at one price.
examples: A {package tour} is easy because everything is booked for you.
wrong: On our package tour we had to book every flight and hotel ourselves.

words.meaning: The busiest time of year for travel, when prices are highest.
examples: Hotels cost twice as much in {peak season}.
wrong: The beach was empty and cheap because it was peak season.

words.meaning: The quiet time of year when few people travel and prices are lower.
examples: We visited in the {off-season} and had the beach to ourselves.
wrong: The town was packed with tourists because it was the off-season.

words.meaning: Describes a holiday price that covers your room, meals and drinks.
examples: Our {all-inclusive} hotel meant we never paid for food.
wrong: The all-inclusive deal meant we paid extra for every meal.

words.meaning: To lie or sit in the sun to get warm or brown.
examples: We spent the afternoon {sunbathing} by the pool.
wrong: He sunbathed in a dark cellar all afternoon.

words.meaning: Sad because you are away from home and miss it.
examples: On my first week abroad I felt very {homesick}.
wrong: She was so homesick that she never once thought about her family.

words.meaning: To travel around a new place to learn about it.
examples: We spent the day {exploring} the old town.
wrong: We explored the city by staying in our hotel room all day.

words.meaning: To take things out of a suitcase or bag and put them away.
examples: As soon as we arrived, I {unpacked} my clothes.
wrong: I unpacked my suitcase by putting all my clothes into it.

words.meaning: Having no free rooms, seats or places left.
examples: Every hotel in town was {fully booked} for the festival.
wrong: The hotel was fully booked, so we got a room easily.

words.meaning: A plan you pay for that gives you money if things go wrong on a trip.
examples: Our {travel insurance} paid for the doctor when I got sick.
wrong: Travel insurance is a ticket that lets you skip the airport queue.

words.meaning: A second plane you take to finish a journey after changing at an airport.
examples: Our first plane was late, and we nearly missed our {connecting flight}.
wrong: We took a connecting flight because the first plane went all the way there.

words.meaning: A short stay in a place between two parts of a long journey.
examples: We had a two-day {stopover} in Singapore on the way to Australia.
wrong: Our stopover was the moment we finally arrived home.

words.meaning: Small bags you are allowed to take with you on a plane.
examples: Keep your passport in your {hand luggage}.
wrong: My hand luggage was too big, so it went under the plane with the suitcases.

words.meaning: A cream you put on your skin to protect it from the sun.
examples: Put on some {sunscreen} before you go to the beach.
wrong: I put on sunscreen so I would burn faster.

words.meaning: A small book of useful sentences in a foreign language for travelers.
examples: I used a {phrasebook} to order food in Italian.
wrong: My phrasebook had only pictures and no words at all.

words.meaning: A person who travels cheaply, carrying their things in a large bag on their back.
examples: The hostel was full of young {backpackers}.
wrong: The backpacker traveled in luxury with ten heavy suitcases.

words.meaning: A visit to a place with a person who shows you around and explains things.
examples: We took a {guided tour} of the museum.
wrong: On the guided tour nobody explained anything to us.

words.meaning: A thin magazine with pictures and information about a product or place.
examples: The hotel {brochure} showed a lovely pool.
wrong: I read the brochure, a thick novel of six hundred pages.

words.meaning: During or for the whole night.
examples: We stayed {overnight} in a small village.
wrong: We stayed overnight and left again before lunch.

words.meaning: The cheapest and most basic seats on a plane.
examples: We flew {economy class} to save money.
wrong: Economy class has the biggest and most expensive seats on the plane.

words.meaning: The place at a border or airport where officials check your passport.
examples: There was a long line at {passport control}.
wrong: At passport control nobody looked at our documents.

words.meaning: Sold without tax, usually at airports.
examples: I bought some {duty-free} perfume at the airport.
wrong: Duty-free goods have extra taxes added to the price.

words.meaning: A hotel room for one person.
examples: I booked a {single room} because I was traveling alone.
wrong: The five of us shared a single room with three beds.

words.meaning: A hotel room with one big bed for two people.
examples: The couple asked for a {double room}.
wrong: A double room has two small beds and is meant for one guest.

words.meaning: A hotel service that brings food and drinks to your room.
examples: We ordered breakfast from {room service}.
wrong: We went down to the restaurant because we wanted room service.

words.meaning: A visit to a place where you go and come back on the same day.
examples: We took a {day trip} to the islands.
wrong: Our day trip lasted for two weeks.

words.meaning: A long journey by car for fun.
examples: We went on a {road trip} across the country.
wrong: Our road trip was a short flight to the capital.

words.meaning: Paying to use a car for a short time.
examples: The airport has a {car rental} desk next to the exit.
wrong: We used car rental because we wanted to buy our own car.

words.meaning: A short holiday away from your normal life.
examples: We planned a weekend {getaway} by the sea.
wrong: Our getaway was a long day of extra work at the office.

words.meaning: To go on a trip with very few bags.
examples: I like to {travel light}, with just one small backpack.
wrong: She likes to travel light, so she packed four huge suitcases.

words.meaning: Feeling ill because of the movement of a boat.
examples: The waves were high, and half the passengers were {seasick}.
wrong: He felt seasick on the train because the sea was so calm.
